form.label: Risk exceptions
form.description: Findings somebody has looked at and decided to handle another way, with what that way is.

div.b: An exception is a decision, not a measurement.
div.span: Everything listed here is still a real vulnerability, still present on the host. It has been taken out of the risk numbers because somebody recorded a reason and a control. That decision is theirs and it is attributed; the counts on Fleet overview always show how many findings are excluded this way, so a quiet dashboard can never be mistaken for a clean fleet. Accepting a risk needs the riskability_accept_risk capability.

search.query: | `riskability_exceptions_now` | where exc_state="active" | stats count AS n

single.option: taken out of every risk number

search.query: | `riskability_exceptions_now` | where exc_state="expired" | stats count AS n

single.option: lapsed; findings are back in the pool

search.query: | `riskability_exceptions_now` | where exc_state="active" AND expires_at!="" AND tonumber(expires_at) < relative_time(now(), "+14d") | stats count AS n

div.span: Select one entry to edit it or return it to the risk pool.

search.query: | `riskability_exceptions_with_counts` | where exc_state="active" | search hostname=$exc_host_tok|s$ OR scope_kind="fleet_cve" | sort 50000 - created_at | table cve_id, scope_label, scope_kind, reason_kind, control, expires_label, findings_covered, hosts_covered, created_by, created_label, notes, exception_key | rename cve_id AS "CVE", scope_label AS "Applies to", scope_kind AS "Scope", reason_kind AS "Reason", control AS "Control in place", expires_label AS "Review by", findings_covered AS "Findings", hosts_covered AS "Hosts", created_by AS "By", created_label AS "Created", notes AS "Notes", exception_key AS "Key"

viz.option: No active exceptions. Every finding the matcher reports is counted in the risk numbers.

div.span: These have lapsed and their findings are counted again. Select one to put it back in force with a new review date.

search.query: | `riskability_exceptions_now` | where exc_state!="active" | search hostname=$exc_host_tok|s$ OR scope_kind="fleet_cve" | eval ended = if(exc_state="revoked", strftime(tonumber(revoked_at), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), expires_label) | sort 50000 - created_at | table exc_state, cve_id, scope_label, reason_kind, control, ended, created_by, notes, exception_key | rename exc_state AS "State", cve_id AS "CVE", scope_label AS "Applies to", reason_kind AS "Reason", control AS "Control in place", ended AS "Ended", created_by AS "By", notes AS "Notes", exception_key AS "Key"

viz.option: Nothing has lapsed or been withdrawn.

search.query: index=`riskability_index_audit` sourcetype=riskability:exception:audit | eval at = strftime(coalesce(when, _time), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | eval covered = coalesce(findings_affected, "") | sort 50000 - _time | table at, action, who, cve_id, hostname, scope_kind, covered, control, changed | rename at AS "When", action AS "Action", who AS "Who", cve_id AS "CVE", hostname AS "Host", scope_kind AS "Scope", covered AS "Findings at the time", control AS "Control in place", changed AS "Changed"

viz.option: No exception activity recorded. This trail is written to an index rather than to the register, so it survives the register being rewritten.

div.b: Why the trail lives in an index.
div.span: A register that can be rewritten by whoever is allowed to write the register is not an audit trail. These events are append-only and kept for five years, because "who accepted this, when, and what did they say they had done instead" is asked long after the finding itself is gone. Expiries are recorded here too, attributed to the scheduler.
